text: Textbooks: where to look next A working bookshelf for this atlas. Choose a book by the question you need to answer; this is a reading guide, not a ranking. Bibliographic years below identify the cited editions, not the invention dates of algorithms. LEARNING RESOURCES公開コード・データ / Public code and data The links lead to publisher records or author-maintained pages. We checked edition metadata and available descriptions or contents, not every derivation in every book. Chapter suggestions describe the atlas connection; they do not claim that all of a textbook has been implemented. A short starting path: Hirsch for the CFD framework; LeVeque for conservation laws and finite-volume reasoning; Toro for Riemann solvers; Patankar for pressure–velocity coupling; Saad for sparse iterative solves. Return to original papers when tracing a particular algorithm. Search the full reference library · All cataloged books · Download BibTeX Covers are supplied by Open Library for the listed ISBN. Each card links to Amazon Japan and the publisher or bibliographic record. The title stays visible when a cover is unavailable. CFD foundations and incompressible flow# Numerical Computation of Internal and External Flows: The Fundamentals of Computational Fluid DynamicsLoading coverCover unavailable Open Library record ISBN 9780750665940 Hirsch# Hirsch, Charles. Numerical Computation of Internal and External Flows: The Fundamentals of Computational Fluid Dynamics. Butterworth-Heinemann, 2007 · edition 2. Use this for the CFD framework: equations, grid properties, consistency, stability, discretization and solution procedures. The cited 2007 book is the second-edition fundamentals volume. Atlas connections: Differences, CFL, von Neumann analysis, and Lax · Structured, unstructured, and triangular meshes · Time integration and leapfrog. J. Computational Techniques for Fluid Dynamics 1: Fundamental and General Techniques. Springer, 1991 · edition 2. Use Volume I for PDE classification, weighted residual methods, steady and diffusion problems, and linear/nonlinear convection. It supplies the common numerical tools before the flow-specific algorithms of Volume II. Atlas connections: Differences, CFL, von Neumann analysis, and Lax · Continuous finite elements: from weak form to sparse assembly · Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration. J. Computational Techniques for Fluid Dynamics 2: Specific Techniques for Different Flow Categories. Springer, 1991 · edition 2. Use Volume II to connect the general techniques of Volume I to different flow-equation categories and their computational solution procedures. Read assumptions and boundary conditions alongside each algorithm. Atlas connections: Incompressible flow: project with compatible discrete operators · Preconditioning, dual time stepping, and residual distribution · Polar and cylindrical coordinates: tensors and viscosity. Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics. Springer, 2020 · edition 4. Use this when connecting discrete operators to a practical CFD solution procedure, especially incompressible pressure–velocity coupling and boundary conditions. Atlas connections: Incompressible flow: project with compatible discrete operators · Polar and cylindrical coordinates: tensors and viscosity. Numerical Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow. CRC Press (current publisher record), 1980. Use this for the physical logic of control-volume balances and SIMPLE-type pressure–velocity coupling. Keep the book exposition separate from the original algorithm papers. Atlas connections: Incompressible flow: project with compatible discrete operators · Euler reconstruction: PPM, characteristics, WENO-Z and AUSM. Finite Volume Methods for Hyperbolic Problems. Cambridge University Press, 2002. Use this for weak solutions, finite-volume reasoning, wave propagation, limiters and multidimensional conservation laws. Companion Clawpack material connects the theory to computation. Atlas connections: Euler reconstruction: PPM, characteristics, WENO-Z and AUSM · Slope limiters: minmod, Superbee, MC, van Leer, and van Albada · Equation gallery: choose the equation before the algorithm. Riemann Solvers and Numerical Methods for Fluid Dynamics: A Practical Introduction. Springer, 2009 · edition 3. Use this when deriving or comparing exact and approximate Euler Riemann solvers, contact waves and high-resolution shock-capturing methods. Atlas connections: Preconditioning, dual time stepping, and residual distribution · Euler reconstruction: PPM, characteristics, WENO-Z and AUSM · Benchmark library. Numerical Approximation of Hyperbolic Systems of Conservation Laws. Springer, 1996 · edition 1. Use this for a mathematical treatment of nonlinear hyperbolic systems and their numerical approximation, including Riemann problems and gas dynamics. Read it alongside LeVeque for finite-volume reasoning and Toro for solver construction. This entry cites the 1996 first edition; a revised second edition appeared in 2021. Atlas connections: Preconditioning, dual time stepping, and residual distribution · Euler reconstruction: PPM, characteristics, WENO-Z and AUSM · A-stability, L-stability and error norms. Finite Difference Methods for Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations: Steady-State and Time-Dependent Problems. SIAM, 2007. Use this for the consistency–stability–convergence chain, ordinary differential equations, boundary-value problems and finite-difference PDE solvers. Atlas connections: A-stability, L-stability and error norms · Time integration and leapfrog · Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration. Use this for conditioning, stable matrix factorizations, least squares and eigenproblems before choosing a solver solely by its name. The author provides the second-edition text and corrections. Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems: Building Blocks for Iterative Methods. SIAM, 1994. Use this open reference as a compact algorithm-and-selection companion for iterative linear solvers, with attention to matrix assumptions. Atlas connections: Sparse and nonlinear systems: measure the actual residual · Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ templates1994 Multigrid: intuition, analysis and implementation# A Multigrid TutorialLoading coverCover unavailable Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780898714623 Briggs · Henson · McCormick / A Multigrid Tutorial# Briggs, William L.; Henson, Van Emden; McCormick, Steve F. A Multigrid Tutorial. SIAM, 2000 · edition 2. Start here for why relaxation damps oscillatory error while coarse grids address the remaining smooth error. Follow the model problems into residual correction, restriction, prolongation and a working multigrid cycle. The second edition also introduces nonlinear problems and AMG. Atlas connections: Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration · Sparse and nonlinear systems: measure the actual residual. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ briggs2000book MultigridLoading coverCover unavailable Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780127010700 Trottenberg · Oosterlee · Schüller / Multigrid# Trottenberg, Ulrich; Oosterlee, Cornelius W.; Schüller, Anton. Multigrid. Academic Press, 2001 · edition 1. Use this as the detailed reference after the tutorial: elementary multigrid theory, local Fourier analysis, smoother and coarse-grid choices, parallel implementation, systems and an AMG appendix. For the atlas Poisson comparison, use it to ask why a cycle converges and how its work changes; AMG, anisotropy and parallel performance need separate implementations and tests. Atlas connections: Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration · Sparse and nonlinear systems: measure the actual residual · Particle gravity: PM, P³M, Tree, multipoles, and multigrid. Atlas connections: Interactive experiment guide · Orthogonal polynomials and mesh basis functions. Use this to connect nodal polynomial bases, quadrature and reference-element operators to DG interface fluxes and PDE algorithms. Atlas connections: Orthogonal polynomials and mesh basis functions · Interactive experiment guide. Geometric Numerical Integration: Structure-Preserving Algorithms for Ordinary Differential Equations. Springer, 2006 · edition 2. Use this for symplectic maps, symmetric compositions, splitting and backward error analysis. Preserving symplectic structure does not mean exactly preserving the original Hamiltonian. Atlas connections: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise · Time integration and leapfrog. Read it alongside the spherical-mesh and variable-staggering notes. Atlas connections: Spherical meshes and Arakawa A, B and C grids · Runge–Kutta families: stages, order, stability, and SSP. The cited original year is 1981; the linked DOI is a later reissue. Atlas connections: Particle gravity: PM, P³M, Tree, multipoles, and multigrid · Gravity kernels: isolated FFTs and a periodic slab. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ hockney1981book Related papers on exact solutions Original article Find an exact traveling wave of Fisher’s equation Ablowitz, Mark J. and Zeppetella, Anthony (1979). Explicit solutions of Fisher’s equation for a special wave speed. Bulletin of Mathematical Biology 41, 835–840. An original article giving exact traveling waves at special speeds of Fisher’s equation. Distinguish these speeds from the general minimal propagation speed when testing reaction–diffusion profiles and fronts. This is a journal article, not a book.
